description: a flying-fish with enlarged pectoral fins that glides above the water

taxon.label: Exocoetidae
taxon.chosen_because: most specific of the taxon words found (subclass of the others)

counts_note: counts are placements in the hierarchy: a tissue or cell type that is part of several organs is counted once per organ. counts_distinct are distinct ontology terms. Use counts_distinct when saying how many tissues or cell types a blueprint has.

pruning.note: The per-parent limits below cap how many organs per system, tissues per organ and cell types per organ enter the blueprint; everything they cut is listed here with the query it came from, so a raised limit reproduces it from the cache. A structure named in the description is never cut: it is added before the limit applies and kept even where Uberon does not class it as an organ. So if the description names a structure and the blueprint lacks it, the limits are not the reason; look at reading.words_not_recognised and reading.conflicts.

honesty: Every node is an existing ontology term; the tool invents no names or identifiers.
Edges are Uberon/CL part_of or subClassOf statements as served by Ubergraph on the retrieval date, including inferred ones.

Taxon constraints (never_in_taxon on the term, its superclasses or its wholes; in_taxon on the term) remove structures the ontology says the taxon cannot have. For non-vertebrates, terms Uberon marks vertebrate_core are removed as well. Absence of a constraint does not mean the taxon has the structure: each organ carries taxon_evidence saying whether Uberon states it for an ancestor of the taxon or merely does not exclude it.

Organ systems and organs are limited to terms Uberon marks in its own core subsets (uberon_slim, efo_slim, vertebrate_core, major_organ, organ_slim); structures named in the description are kept regardless.
Organs are ranked major organs first, then by how many cell types the Cell Ontology records for them, which measures curation effort, not biology.
Links from a function word to a structure come either from the ontology (capable_of, reported as such) or from the hand-written lexicon (reported as curated).

A description is read at the most specific lexicon entry that matches it, longest phrase first; a shorter reading wholly inside a longer one is recorded under reading.anatomy_words_subsumed instead of being added again.

Words the lexicon does not know are listed under reading.words_not_recognised. The tool reads a word list, not English: an unrecognised word means the blueprint says nothing about whatever that word named.

Everything the per-parent limits cut is listed under "pruning", and structures named in the description are never cut. A named structure absent from the blueprint was either unrecognised or taxon-excluded, and both are reported.
The genome sketch is marker gene products from the Cell Ontology, not a genome.
Descriptions that resolve inside the held-out clade are refused and leave no file behind; the check and its query are recorded under "holdout" for every built blueprint.

genome_sketch.label: SKETCH
genome_sketch.note: Not a genome. These are marker gene products (Protein Ontology terms) that the Cell Ontology or its Provisional Cell Ontology extension records as expressed by the listed cell types (relation RO_0002292 "expresses"), reduced to the most specific term per cell. Most cell types carry no such annotation, so absence means nothing. Predicting a genome from a description is out of scope and would be labelled a sketch too.

kernelChecked: Every part_of edge goes from a strictly deeper level to a shallower one (Graph.LevelsDown), so the part_of relation is acyclic: no term is transitively part of itself (Graph.acyclic_of_levelsDown).
The transitive closure of the stated edges is transitive and strictly decreases the level (Graph.transGen_trans, Graph.transGen_level_lt).
Every edge joins two nodes of the graph and every node other than the body root has a whole, hence every node reaches the body root: no orphans (Graph.rooted_of).

No never_in_taxon statement pinned from Ubergraph on a kept term, a superclass or a whole names a taxon containing the blueprint taxon; every in_taxon and stated_in_taxon statement names a containing taxon (TaxonData.Ok).
Nodes are distinct terms (List.nodup_range) and the distinct counts per level are body 1, organ_system 13, organ 67, tissue 198, cell 257; the file holds 674 placements.
assumed: That Uberon and the Cell Ontology are correct and that Ubergraph served their part_of, subClassOf, never_in_taxon and in_taxon statements correctly and completely on the retrieval dates; the graph and the taxon rows are data whose hashes and queries are pinned here.
That the five levels are the right notion of depth; the theorems use only that edges strictly decrease it.

certificate.covers_note: The certificate is about the whole graph: acyclicity, rootedness, taxon consistency and the per-level counts are properties of the node set and the edge set together, so every node is inside its scope.

fixes: Gene keys: Bgee Ensembl ids absent from ZFIN's 1:1 table are merged onto the ZFIN gene with the identical symbol (summary.gene_id_rules); fgf10a and shha no longer appear twice.

Experimental condition: phenotype rows are kept only under ZFIN 'standard conditions' (ZECO:0000103), matched through phenotype_fish.txt and pheno_environment_fish.txt. The clean file turned out to be almost entirely standard conditions already; what is rejected is mostly annotations that ZFIN also recorded under a treatment experiment and that the join cannot tell apart (ambiguous), plus a few uniquely non-standard rows (summary.zfin_phenotype.rejected, conditions_of_rejected_rows, which lists every condition among the candidate experiments of rejected rows, standard conditions included).

Loss of function: every 'required for' phenotype link carries loss_of_function_evidence; homozygous alleles that also have a heterozygous phenotype and no truncating consequence are rejected as 'loss of function not established' instead of being typed 'required for'.
lat4a = slc43a2a settled on two records (fin_size.verified_leads[2].symbol_check); the aliases check now reads the symbol column.
still_open: ZFIN records attach only where the blueprint has a node with an ontology cross-reference; 16 of 257 cell types have a ZFA equivalent, so the cell layer is capped by the crosswalk.
Bgee links carry no stage (anatomy-only call file). Body-level Bgee links are whole-organism samples, real but not body-plan evidence.
GO system mapping misses musculoskeletal, integumental and other systems (no GO term 'results in development of' their Uberon term).
No ZP identifiers; ZFIN EQ annotations stand in. No medaka phenotype source.

slimming.rule: direct links only, one row per gene symbol, organism and evidence kind, at most 40 per link type per node (sufficient, required, then expressed in by evidence kind), the same rule as dashboard/build-graph.mjs; per-node counts in nodes are complete

genotype.constraint: Almost no molecular data exists for flying fish (Exocoetidae). NCBI holds one scaffold-level assembly (GCA_018398805.1, Hirundichthys speculiger) and OrthoDB holds no genome for the whole suborder Belonoidei. Every gene link here was measured in a PROXY species, zebrafish (Danio rerio) or medaka (Oryzias latipes, same order Beloniformes as flying fish). None of it is flying-fish data.
genotype.causation_warning: Most links are 'expressed in': the gene's RNA or protein was detected in the structure. That is not causation. 'required for' means a single-gene loss-of-function zebrafish has an abnormal phenotype there (or, for GO-based links, that GO places the gene in the structure's developmental process on mutant evidence). 'sufficient for' here means a verified gain-of-function allele changes the structure (e.g. enlarges it); it does not mean the gene makes the structure. No gene 'makes' a fin.

propagation_rules.expressed in: propagates UP part_of: expression in a part implies some expression in what contains it. Marked derived with the path.
propagation_rules.required for: never propagates DOWN. Propagation UP is an inference, marked derived, never presented as observed.
propagation_rules.graph: the blueprint's own part_of placements (organism-design/examples/a-flying-fish.json), which the lean thread kernel-certified as acyclic and rooted, so propagation is well defined and terminates. Bgee's own propagation is excluded: only Bgee calls that include data observed in that very structure are used.

not_sourced: Any flying-fish (Exocoetidae) expression or phenotype record: none exists in Bgee or ZFIN.
Medaka phenotypes: no medaka phenotype database was queried; medaka links are Bgee expression only.
Bgee SPARQL endpoint: refused (HTTP 403, a Cloudflare challenge page); Bgee bulk call files were used instead.
Bgee REST expr_calls page: HTTP 200 with no expression calls for the parameters tried.
Stage for Bgee links: the anatomy-only call files merge stages; Bgee links carry no stage.
ZP term identifiers: ZFIN's EQ annotations (ZFA + PATO) were used; they were not converted to ZP IDs.

summary.storage: map.json stores in full: every 'required for' and 'sufficient for' link, every link in the pectoral-fin subtree, every link of the focus and fin-size genes, and the Cell Ontology marker links. All other direct 'expressed in' links are in genotype/expression_index.json.gz.

fin_size.why: Fin presence is generic to fish; what is distinctive in flying fish is the size and proportion of the paired fins. Fin size is an organ-level proportion, which connects to Thompson's scaling claims; no scaling is computed here.

verified_leads.finding: Gain-of-function mutations in the potassium channel kcnk5b (the 'another longfin' mutant) give proportionally enlarged fins in zebrafish.
verified_leads.link_type: sufficient for (an increase in fin size, not for making a fin)

verified_leads.finding: The classic longfin (t2) mutant is a regulatory kcnh2a allele that overexpresses this potassium channel and elongates the fins.
verified_leads.link_type: sufficient for (fin overgrowth); not attached to a blueprint node because ZFIN does not record the longfin phenotype under a single-gene kcnh2a fish

verified_leads.organism: 35 flying-fish and related species (phylogenomics) plus zebrafish (genetics)
verified_leads.finding: A phylogenomic study of flying fishes found signatures of convergent paired-fin enlargement and, intersected with zebrafish fin-size mutants, implicated lat4a and kcnh2a.
verified_leads.link_type: association (comparative genomics), plus zebrafish genetics; not a measurement in a flying-fish fin

verified_leads.finding: kcnk5b integrates calcineurin's effect on fin allometry.

zfin_fin_size_genes.definition: zebrafish genes with an abnormal ZFIN phenotype whose structure is a fin or part of one (ZFA 'fin' part_of/is_a closure) and whose quality is a size or length (PATO increased/decreased length, size, width or height). Any allele type, any zygosity; GOF and LOF are not separated here.
